History.PlayerOk: Tell me about the Klissan War
History.SB: Today we can offer you a free presentation on the history of the Klissan War. An aspiring ranger ought to know their history.
History.SBOk: Gaals were the first to encounter the klissan -- this happened many centuries before their contact with the other Coalition races. Back then the gaalian civilization didn't consider territorial greed as a sign of barbarity, or introspection and moderation as wisdom, pursuing a policy of active galactic expansion. Having settled numerous worlds in adjacent sectors, the gaals wanted to reach the next spiral arm of the Galaxy. This was considered unfeasible, as entering and exiting the hyperspace is only possible in places where the continuum is distorted by the gravitational pull of particularly massive objects, such as stars.  Moreover, "penetrating" the continuum between the two zones consumes energy, more of it as the distance increases. In contrast, spiral arms are separated by countless parsecs of emptiness; to penetrate them in one trip you'd need a truly colossal supply of energy, perhaps that of an entire star. Sure, you could also follow the spiral: the local arm to the center of the Galaxy, then back along the next, but that kind of journey is too long even for gaals to undertake. So the gaals chose a third option, made possible by the new technology of stable "bubbles" of distorted space, capable of teleportation independent of the mass that generates them. Such a "bubble" has made it possible to travel virtually anywhere in the known cosmos.
SBOk1: The gaals promptly used it to reach the neighboring arm and found the first colonies in the system of a star they went on to call Elthane. From there their expansion proceeded smoothly, until one of the fleets tasked with exploring the second arm had a chance encounter with Makhpella. Makhpella was a giant sentient ship -- a product of abiological evolution. She was moving from one star to another with an entourage of her own -- a fleet of smaller subordinate "ships," called the klissan. That first encounter ended in tragedy, with the klissan destroying the entire gaalian expedition. And so began the war, in which the gaals suffered one defeat after another. And it wasn't just their fleet detachments that were perishing: Makhpella and the klissan would wipe out every living creature on every colonized planet they could reach...

The gaals that had stayed behind in our spiral arm were spared this awful fate, but the shock of it all had steered the course of their civilization in a completely new direction. Further expansion in space has become far less popular than before. The bubble-generating technologies were outlawed and classified to all but the highest echelons of government. The damages to science and other intellectual pursuits were equally great, as many scholars and scientists had rushed into the new arm, eager to explore the new frontier, and were now dead.
SBOk2: In the centuries that followed the gaalian civilization began to gradually recover, getting back to space exploration, establishing contact with the fae, the pelengs, the maloqs and the humans, and assisting in the formation of the Galactic Council. And then, three hundred years ago, when it seemed as though a time for lasting peace has come, Rachehan came and ruined everything. Formerly one of the top commanders in the peleng fleet, he became incensed when he was passed over for a promotion and decided to turn to piracy. Before making his move official, he went to work for the national intelligence agency, where he came across an old gaalian archive that had been long forgotten by everybody else. Upon learning about the secret of "bubbles" and Makhpella, he theorized (correctly, as it turned out!) that there were many such Makhpellas out there. Of course, he had little need of Makhpella initially. The bubble technology was more than sufficient to pirate all over the known space with impunity, emerging anywhere at will and disappearing back into hyperspace.

Desperate, the five civilizations formed a common anti-terrorist strike force which managed to lure the pirate fleet into a trap. It was a massacre, but Rachehan still managed to escape with his life. It was then that he decided to fly to the adjacent spiral arm and seek out Makhpella, aiming to either gain control over the superweapon or set it on the united governments' forces. As you might expect, plan A didn't quite work out for him. Plan B, however, worked out beautifully, as Makhpella and the klissan chased him right into our spiral arm.
History.SBOk3: As the second war waged on, it was hardly more successful than the first. Though five civilizations were putting up a better fight against the klissan than the gaals alone, they were still losing, however gradually. And so the five races gambled on the rangers, hoping that small autonomous vessels would succeed where massive fleets had failed -- get close to Makhpella and destroy her. Funny how the military always strives to destroy the enemy, rather than try and understand their motives... Fortunately, there were those in the scientific community who aspired for the latter. Little did they know that they had a champion among the rangers, shrewd enough to use the latest technologies to establish direct contact with Makhpella. Amazingly, it turned out that Makhpella never meant anybody harm! The Makhpella race is inorganic in nature, having emerged from the gas-and-dust nebulae in space; their bodies constitute a myriad tiny crystalline elements, combining in different forms when placed in an energy field. And the klissan (contrary to the initial theory that they were her subjects or offspring) turned out to be remotely controlled organs which Makhpella could cultivate in great numbers. Makhpellas travel through space, feeding on the energy of stars and showing very little interest in planets. This interest was further diminished after a visit to a random planet proved catastrophic -- the native bacteria entered the organism and proceeded to destroy Makhpella crystals as it spread. Consequently, when the first and the second Makhpella encountered our civilizations, they mistook the lifeless spaceships for sentient beings, and the crews manning them for organic parasites!  Makhpellas never even considered the possibility that organic life could be intelligent. As such, their cause was a noble one: to stop the organic plague from spreading...
SBOk4: Once the misunderstanding was clarified, Makhpellas were no longer a threat. They live in their own arm of the Galaxy, while we live in ours. Wicked tongues have dubbed that war the War of Delusion... And rightfully so, seeing as our governments try their damnedest to avoid any mention of it...
But now you also know everything there is to know about that war, <Player>. Perhaps this knowledge will prove useful to you in the future.
